lead: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy is acute liver failure from microvesicular fat in liver cells, in the third trimester or just after birth. It is rare (about 1 in 10 000) but deadly: an obstetric emergency treated by stabilising and delivering.
f: Twins, male fetus (about 3 : 1), coexisting mild PE, first pregnancy, low BMI · Fault in mitochondrial fatty-acid oxidation, often a fetal LCHAD deficiency

sc: AFLP mother; newborn later has low glucose → Test the baby for LCHAD deficiency

f: Days of nausea, vomiting, malaise · Epigastric or RUQ pain · Jaundice, headache · Polyuria, polydipsia (transient diabetes insipidus) · Confusion → coma · Mild hypertension ± proteinuria

Hypoglycaemia: check often · PT/INR raised, fibrinogen low → DIC · Bilirubin raised; ALT/AST moderately raised (usually under 1000) · Marked hyperuricaemia, raised creatinine · WBC raised; platelets low (milder than HELLP) · Acidosis, raised ammonia and lactate · Ultrasound: bright liver; mainly to exclude others · Swansea criteria: 6 or more of 14 features

sc: Jaundice, glucose 40 mg/dL, INR 2 at 35 wk → AFLP

f: Fulminant liver failure, DIC, PPH, AKI, hypoglycaemic coma, pancreatitis · Maternal death about 18%, fetal death about 23% · Baby with LCHAD defect: hypoglycaemia, cardiomyopathy

Trimester is the first clue · Hyperemesis: early, vomiting, mild ALT rise · Cholestasis: itch, well, bile acids raised · HELLP: high BP, low platelets, LDH raised · AFLP: ill, vomiting, low glucose, raised INR · Hepatitis E: any trimester, ALT over 1000, IgM

tr: Hepatitis E is mild in non-pregnant adults but causes fulminant liver failure in the third trimester (death up to 20%)

f: HDU/ICU with a team; inform a liver unit · 10–50% dextrose, glucose every 1–2 h · Clotting: IV vitamin K 10 mg, FFP, cryoprecipitate, platelets before delivery · Strict fluid balance; treat hypertension · Deliver once stable, whatever the gestation (usually CS) · No regional block if platelets below 80 or clotting deranged · Most recover within days; may recur (test parents and baby for LCHAD)

sc: Ill, jaundiced, vomiting at 36 wk → Check glucose, INR, platelets and BP first
